name: Ram
overview: Ram was a male descendant of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the firstborn son of Jerahmeel. His role is primarily genealogical, marking him as an important link in the lineage recorded in Scripture. There are no additional notes or narrative details about his life.
namesAndTitles: The name Ram is a proper name meaning 'high' or 'exalted.' This meaning reflects a positive attribute but was not explicitly given by God. The name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 2:25.
familyAndRelationships: Ram is explicitly recorded as the son of Jerahmeel. Additionally, he is inferred to be the father of Maaz, Jamin, and Eker based on genealogical listings. Scripture does not provide further familial details beyond these relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Ram's significance lies in his place within the genealogical records of Judah, serving as a foundational figure in the ancestry that Scripture carefully preserves. His identification as the firstborn son of Jerahmeel situates him within the broader narrative of Israel's tribal history. While no direct narrative actions are attributed to him, his genealogical role contributes to the continuity of the biblical record.
